headline: Dozens injured in clash between former employees and customer forum at Islami Bank head office
summary: Protests by sacked Islami Bank employees demanding reinstatement turned violent outside the bank's Dhaka head office. Dozens were injured as two groups clashed, with both sides blaming each other for the violence.
details: A clash erupted yesterday between former employees of Islami Bank Bangladesh PLC and members of a customer forum outside the bank's head office in Dhaka's Motijheel area. The two groups had gathered for separate programs, which quickly escalated into a physical confrontation.

The former employees, allegedly recruited after the S Alam Group took over the bank in 2017, were terminated by the interim government and are demanding their jobs back. The "Sachetan Grahak Forum" (Conscious Customer Forum) has been actively opposing their reinstatement.

Both factions have accused each other of initiating the violence. Shahidul Islam, a representative of the sacked employees, claimed that 25 of their members were injured and admitted to Dhaka Medical College Hospital. He stated their peaceful demonstration was attacked by the consumer forum members.

Conversely, Nuru-Un-Nabi Manik, president of the Sachetan Grahak Forum, asserted that around 30 of their members sustained injuries, with five in serious condition. He alleged that the sacked employees attacked them during a peaceful protest and accused them of trying to destabilize the bank.

Manik further claimed that the attack occurred with police protection, a statement that could not be immediately verified as the Motijheel Police Station's officer-in-charge was unavailable for comment.

headline_marked: MMCH fire: Officials [[investigating death reports]] amid panic and injuries
headline: MMCH fire: Officials investigating death reports amid panic and injuries
summary: Panic erupted at Mymensingh Medical College Hospital after a fire broke out in the new building. While officials are investigating reports of fatalities, several patients and their relatives sustained injuries during the chaotic evacuation.
details: A fire incident at the new building of Mymensingh Medical College Hospital (MMCH) on Monday evening caused panic among patients and their relatives. While the fire department quickly brought the blaze under control, initial reports of fatalities are being investigated by hospital authorities and divisional officials.

The fire, believed to have started from an electrical short circuit in the lift control room of the eight-story building, led to smoke spreading across several floors. This caused significant alarm, prompting patients and visitors to evacuate via the staircases.

Divisional Commissioner SM Humayun Kabir Sarkar stated that no evidence of deaths due to stampedes or the fire itself has been found so far. He urged for confirmed evidence before disseminating unverified information, noting that lists from the emergency department and morgue are being cross-referenced.

However, some patients' relatives reported injuries sustained during the hurried evacuation. One resident mentioned that his daughters and granddaughters were hurt while descending the stairs, as some stairwell exits were reportedly locked.

The fire, reported at 5:55 PM, was extinguished by 6:30 PM with the help of ten fire units. The primary cause is suspected to be an electrical short circuit, but a formal investigation is underway to determine the exact origin. The lack of adequate emergency exits and preparedness in the new building has also come under scrutiny.

Officials, including the Divisional Commissioner, DIG of Mymensingh Range, Deputy Commissioner, and Superintendent of Police, held a meeting and inspected the site to assess the situation and verify casualty figures.
